answer: A refundable identity bond plus slow, earned throughput resists Sybils. Creating an identity locks a bond, returned only after sustained honest work, so spawning thousands of fakes means funding thousands of bonds at once. Each new identity starts with a narrow river of permitted transactions that widens only as verified work accumulates. Like timber framing on a basalt foundation, it is cheap to check but costly to duplicate at scale, turning a cheap Sybil flood into a slow, expensive, rate-limited investment.
